main_text.p: similarium & difsimilarium actiones non differre, si omnes nostri corporis partes ita agunt, sicut struthiocameli uenter, cuius actio semper est uniuoca. Quantum autem inter se discrepent omniū nostri corporis partium actiones, iudicent medicinæ tyrones. Nam quemadmodum actionum læsio est duplex, quarum una ad animalem, altera ad naturalem functionem pertinet: ita duplices numerantur actiones, naturalis uidelicet, & animalis, quemadmodum often dit Galenus libro de Differentijs symptomatum. His adde quòd tot sunt actionum differentiæ, quot sunt nostri corporis partium genera. At alias esse similares, alias dissimilares & compositas nemine medicum latet. Quamuis similares partes intellexerit, quibus solis uis alimentum concoquendi & assimilandi sit, non tamen ipsum alimentum pariter coficiunt. Longè enim aliter hepar & uenæ coquunt, quàm uentriculus & uenæ portæ. Deinde postrema concoctio, quæ quidem in habitu corporis peragitur, & assimilatio ab aliis alimenti mutationibus non parum inter se discrepant. page.notes: The word "often" in the line "quemadmodum often dit Galenus" is printed as "often" in the scan, reading "quemadmodum osten" is not clear; the printed word appears to be "often" with a long-s spelling "ofte" and is uncertain. Lines are rendered as paragraph flow; the hyphenated line-end words "concoc-tio" appear as "concoctio" and "pera-gitur" as "peragitur" in the printing. The printed line ending "stru-" continues on the next page as "thio-". The right-margin word "thio-" is a catchword-like continuation and is kept as a note. Text "alimenti mutationibus" and "uentriculus" read as printed. Two printing irregularities: "uenter, cuius" at the start and "uenæ" repeated are as printed; no corrections applied.
